summary: Bocoles with spicy sweet potatoes, adapted from Diana Kennedy's My Mexico: masa and refried black bean cakes fried about 3 minutes per side, topped with sautéed sweet potato, jalapeno and New Mexico chile and crema; serves 6 in 40 minutes as a vegetarian entree.
glance: 2 1/2 cups masa harina, 1 1/2 cups + 2 tablespoons warm water, 2 cups refried black beans, baking powder
golf-ball balls pressed 1/4 inch thick, about 3 minutes per side
faq: What are bocoles?

Little pan-fried cakes of masa and mashed black beans, typically served as an antojito (appetizer). They fry up with a crispy exterior and a somewhat creamy inside; the crust is a bit like an Indian dosa's.
Are sweet potatoes the same as yams?
They aren't even related, but you may find sweet potatoes labeled yams in your grocery. The ones to use have a dark orange-brown skin and orange flesh.
What if I don't have refried black beans?
Cook half an onion and 2 cloves of garlic in a couple tablespoons of oil, add cooked black beans and a little oil, and mash to a smooth puree, adding water as needed. Season to taste.
Can I make the dough ahead?
Yes, the dough can be refrigerated overnight after you mix in the refried beans and baking powder.
What do I serve with bocoles?
Shredded romaine, crema, optional pomegranate seeds, and a jicama, radish and orange salad, guacamole or salsa. The author's kids love them and call them "yummy cakes."

summary: Veggie chili beans with cornbread dumplings: pinto beans, onion, fire-roasted tomatoes and chipotle veggie sausage heated in a casserole at 400°F, topped with golf-ball-sized spoonfuls of cornmeal dumpling batter and baked about 20 minutes uncovered; serves 4 as a comfort-food main.
glance: 400°F, about 20 minutes uncovered, until the dumplings are golden and baked through
3/4 cup cornmeal, 1/4 cup flour, yogurt, milk, egg and oil
Vegetarian; not vegan or gluten-free but could be adjusted
faq: What is the idea behind this dish?

Comfort food with a biscuit or dumpling top: the author's wife wished he'd make more comfort food, so he dropped a simple cornbread batter on a casserole of beans, onions and veggie sausage. It involves more canned food than he usually uses, but came out tasty.
What vegetarian sausage did the author use?
Field Roast Mexican Chipotle vegetarian sausage (kinda spicy), two links, or 8 ounces of another veggie meat cut into bite-size chunks.
How do I make the dumplings?

Mix the dry ingredients (cornmeal, flour, baking powder, salt) in one bowl and beat the yogurt, milk, egg and oil in another, then quickly mix without overbeating. Drop chunks a bit smaller than a golf ball on the hot casserole, leaving spaces between them.
How do I know the dumplings are done?
After about 20 minutes uncovered, the beans are hot and the dumplings are golden brown and baked through; check with a toothpick if unsure.
What do I serve with it?
Grated cheddar, Louisiana hot sauce, and a quick salad of diced cucumbers and radishes with dill, parsley, mint and a lime dressing.

summary: Caramelized cauliflower frittata: florets sauteed in olive oil until deeply browned, mixed with 10 eggs, cream, 1/2 cup of minced fresh herbs and lemon zest in a 12-inch skillet, started on the stove and baked at 350°F covered until fully set; serves 4 as an entree or 8 as a first course.
glance: 4 as a light entree or 8 as a first course
10 large eggs with 3/4 cup cream or milk
1/2 cup packed leafy herbs (parsley, thyme, marjoram, a little mint)
350°F, covered with foil, 15 minutes to an hour until fully set
yield: 4 as a light entree or 8 as a first course
faq: Why caramelize the cauliflower?

Cauliflower has a split personality: boiled or steamed it's cabbagey, bland and slightly bitter, but roasted or sauteed until it has lots of dark brown caramelized spots it becomes luscious, savory and craveable. The frittata emphasizes that flavor.
How much herb should I use?
About 1/2 cup of packed leafy herbs, less if they are very intense like tarragon. Don't use anywhere near that much of something woody like rosemary.
How do I cook the frittata?

After mixing the cauliflower with the eggs, either start cooking the eggs on the stove over a medium flame until beginning to set and finish covered in the oven, or do the whole thing in the oven; the author lately prefers letting the oven do more of the work.
How do I avoid rubbery eggs?
Get them fully cooked and not runny, but not far past that. Cool the skillet and cauliflower a bit before adding the eggs so they don't overcook on contact.
How should I serve it?

Room temperature or cold is the author's favorite, though piping hot can be good; just warm with a bracing salad it makes a great light lunch, or cut it into bite-sized pieces on baguette slices with aioli and pickled onions as a party snack.

summary: Kitchen sink spaghetti: eggplant, asparagus, red onion, roasted red peppers, garlic jam, chipotle and white wine cooked into a thick sauce, then combined with spaghetti and reserved pasta water and finished with basil, lemon zest, smoked mozzarella, pepper and toasted pepitas; serves 4.
glance: 1 pound spaghetti, drained when nearly done but definitely al dente
6 cloves garlic, red onion, 2 tablespoons roasted garlic and onion jam, 1 mashed chipotle, 1/2 cup white wine
basil, lemon zest, 1/2 pound smoked mozzarella, black pepper, 1/2 cup pepitas
Vegetarian; vegan if you omit the cheese
faq: What is in kitchen sink spaghetti?

Asparagus, roasted red peppers, eggplant, red onion, garlic, white wine, Stonewall Kitchen's roasted garlic and onion jam, basil, rosemary, lemon zest, pumpkin seeds, smoked mozzarella and chipotle: the author calls it about as far from traditional as he goes, and really tasty.
Why add chipotle and smoked mozzarella?
Italian dishes often have red pepper flakes, and the chipotle and smoked mozzarella bring some of the smoky flavors an omnivore might introduce with bacon.
What is the garlic and onion jam for?
A tablespoon or two melted into the base of a sauce is an incredible, complex-tasting alternative to slow, low caramelization of onions you do yourself.
How do I bring the sauce and pasta together?

The sauce will seem too thick; cook the pasta, add the vegetables back to the pan after the pasta has cooked about 5 minutes, then toss the nearly done pasta with the pan contents and some of the reserved pasta water over medium-low heat. The starchy, salty, sweet water thins the sauce without greatly diluting the flavors.
Can I use other nuts?
Pepitas are used because nuts aren't allowed in the author's house, but walnuts, hazelnuts or pine nuts would be even better.

summary: Kaffir (makrut) lime dipping sauce, a vegetarian take on nuoc cham: water, sugar, 6 kaffir lime leaves, salt and chili flakes brought to a boil and steeped 15 minutes, then mixed with rice vinegar and tamari; yields about 1 cup for spring rolls or rice bowls.
glance: bring to a boil, then steep 15 minutes, remove the leaves, cool
sweet, sour, spicy, salty and citrus
Vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free with a wheat-free soy sauce
faq: What is the sauce for?
It's similar to a vegetarian version of Vietnamese nuoc cham, suitable for serving with spring rolls or pouring over a rice bowl.
Is "kaffir lime" the right name?
Kaffir lime is considered an offensive term, although it is by far the most commonly used name for the plant; makrut lime is more acceptable, though the author has never actually heard it used.
What does the leaf taste like and what can I substitute?
The leaf infuses a big, round citrus flavor without any acidity. The closest substitution is probably normal lime rind, but it is by no means the same.
Where do I find the leaves?
At a good Asian specialty market, especially one with a Southeast Asian selection, or an Indian grocery.
How do I balance the sauce?
Once mixed, give it a good taste and adjust any component: you should be able to clearly taste all of them except the tamari.
What variations work?
Add some or all of finely sliced scallions, ginger, garlic or cilantro; replace the rice vinegar with a coconut or citrus vinegar; use a minced fresh chili in place of the chili flakes.

summary: Grapefruit and avocado crudo: red grapefruit squared off and sliced into 1/3-inch slabs (or cut into supremes), each topped with avocado, chervil and soaked capers and finished with olive oil, sea salt and pepper; serves 4 in 15 minutes, assembled at the last minute.
glance: 2 red, cut into 1/3-inch slabs; about 5-6 usable slices each
at the last minute; the grapefruit can be cut ahead and refrigerated
faq: How do I cut the grapefruit into slabs?

Use an extremely sharp chef's knife: remove about 1/2 inch from the top and bottom, then resting on the bottom make four vertical cuts to produce a rough cube, removing all of the skin and pith, and slice vertically into 1/3-inch slabs avoiding the core.
Is there an easier way to cut grapefruit?
If you don't care about thin slices, cut it into supremes: remove the top, bottom and skin, then working over a bowl insert the knife next to each membrane to free the segments.
Can I make it ahead?

Don't put it together in advance, because the grapefruit will start to break down into a juicy mess on the plate. You can cut the grapefruit ahead and refrigerate it in a covered bowl, but wait until the last minute to assemble.
What do I do with the leftover grapefruit?
Slicing this way produces a lot of waste, so juice the rest for a cook's treat.
How do I prepare the capers?
Briefly soak them to remove some salt, then drain.

summary: Enfrijoladas de espinaca: corn tortillas dipped 5-10 seconds in hot spicy black bean soup (used as the sauce), filled with a quick spinach, onion and cumin saute and topped with cotija, avocado and cilantro; serves 4 in 15 minutes.
glance: 1 quart spicy black bean soup, heated
Vegetarian and gluten-free; vegan if you omit the cheese
faq: What are enfrijoladas?

A simple, homey Mexican dish rarely seen in the United States: corn tortillas dipped in a smooth bean sauce spiked with a few chiles, served simply with more sauce and cheese or crema, or filled. Think of them like spinach enchiladas with beans instead of tomatoes or tomatillos as the sauce backbone.
How do I make them in 15 minutes?

Use a ready-made creamy black bean soup that is already the perfect consistency and flavor for the sauce (the author used Pacific Natural Foods' Spicy Black Bean Soup, an advertiser), plus a quick spinach saute.
How do I dip the tortillas?
Carefully dip each tortilla in the hot soup using tongs, holding it 5-10 seconds until it has softened but isn't falling apart, then fill with about 3 tablespoons of spinach and loosely roll.
How do I cook the spinach filling?
Defrost 1 pound of frozen spinach and squeeze out some water, saute onion and garlic 2 minutes, add the spinach, cumin, oregano and salt and cook, stirring, 3 minutes.
How do I make it vegan or gluten-free?
Omit or replace the cotija for vegan; double-check the corn tortilla ingredients for gluten-free.

summary: Crispy soba noodle pancakes: cooked, cooled soba tossed with sesame seeds and pressed into handfuls in 1/8 inch of hot oil, fried a minute or two per side with no egg or binder, and served with scallions, cucumber, sesame oil and a gochujang-mirin dip; makes about 8.
glance: 1/3 pound dry soba, cooked and cooled
1/8 inch of oil just short of smoking, a minute or two per side
1/2 cup gochujang whisked with mirin (or rice vinegar)
faq: Do soba pancakes need egg or a binder?
The author hoped they'd form a pancake without egg or any other binder so the noodles could crisp without burning the egg, and it worked great: the noodles locked together beautifully.
How do I fry them?

Bring about 1/8 inch of oil to frying temperature over medium-high heat, just short of smoking. Put a handful of noodles combined with sesame seeds in the skillet and press to flatten, fry until golden brown on one side, a minute or two, flip and fry the other side, then drain and season with sea salt.
What is gochujang?

Korean chili paste, also spelled kochujang: not extremely hot, usually including fermented soybeans and rice for a complex, appetizing flavor, compared by the author to chilis mixed with miso. Sriracha makes another kind of chili sauce if you can't find it.
How should I serve them?
As an appetizer or bar snack with cold sake or beer. It's messy eating as the crispy, salty noodles break up, so not for hand-passing to people in party dresses.
Where do the noodles come from?
The author made them from leftovers from his Japanese-style soba noodle soup.

summary: A reimagined fruit salad made entirely of fruit (including the culinary-vegetable ones: olives, tomatoes, avocado), served with a lime isomalt glass, black olive puree, pressed avocado squares and peeled red globe grapes dipped in malic acid powder; a modernist plate for 4.
glance: lime isomalt glass, black olive puree, avocado squares, peeled grapes with malic acid powder
30 grams, melted in a 300°F oven and topped with lime zest
faq: What is the idea behind this fruit salad?

Everything on the plate is fruit, playing with ingredients that are technically fruit but thought of more as vegetable (olives, tomatoes, avocado). You can eat the combinations "safe" (avocado with lime, tomatoes with olives) or play a little: grape with avocado, blood orange with tomato gel.
Why serve the grapes with malic acid powder?

Instant apple cider mix is just sugar and malic acid, which tastes like slightly puckery apple candy. Serve the peeled red globe grapes on a small pile of the powder for diners to dip like Lik-M-Aid, since the powder gets moist quickly and wouldn't work rolled on the grapes in the salad.
What is isomalt?

A sugar-like ingredient great where you want less sweetness, no browning and resistance to absorbing moisture. Here it is made into a powder, sieved into a thin layer and baked at 300°F until just melted to make a lime glass.
How do I make the avocado squares?

Brush lime juice on plastic wrap, scoop avocado onto it, add more lime juice, cover with more plastic and press and roll to an even layer a generous 1/8 inch thick without voids. Cut four 3-inch squares and refrigerate.
What do papaya seeds taste like?
The author says they have a surprising flavor reminiscent of horseradish.

summary: Chanterelles with a corn sauce and Asian pear slaw: corn kernels and ginger pureed and strained, then thickened with butter into a velvety sauce; browned chanterelles served on it with a quick slaw of Asian pear, red onion and sesame oil; serves 4 as an appetizer in 30 minutes.
glance: kernels from 2 ears, pureed a couple of minutes, strained, simmered with butter until pudding-like
12 ounces chanterelles, fried about 5 minutes until browned
Vegetarian and gluten-free; vegan if you omit or replace the butter
faq: Where does the corn sauce idea come from?

Grant Achatz famously made a corn sauce in sheet form by cooking pureed corn kernels until the natural starch thickens the juice, then freezing it in a thin sheet to drape over a dish. The author uses the first part and serves the sauce directly, skipping the potentially hairy freezing and peeling off wax paper.
How do I make the corn sauce?

Puree the corn kernels, ginger, 1/2 teaspoon sugar and 1/2 teaspoon salt for a good couple of minutes, strain very thoroughly through cheesecloth or sieves to extract all the liquid, then simmer the liquid with butter over low heat, whisking; it thickens rapidly, then cook 2 more minutes. It should have the texture of pudding.
What if the sauce is too thick?
Add water, a tablespoon at a time.
What does the slaw do?
The quick slaw of Asian pear (apple-pear) with red onion, sesame oil and lime juice adds crunch and sweetness. You could serve it with almost any kind of fritter or even on a fusion taco.
Why chanterelles with corn and ginger?
The author loves chanterelles with corn and corn with ginger, and by the "transitive property of delicio-algebraics" put all three together.
